cases.title: Skyward Airlines: Declining Profitability
cases.summary: A regional airline's operating profit has fallen 40% in two years despite flat revenue. Find the driver and recommend a fix.

prompt.context: Skyward Airlines is a mid-sized carrier operating 60 routes across the northeastern United States. Over the last two years, revenue has stayed roughly flat at $1.2B per year, but operating profit has dropped from $150M to $90M — a 40% decline. The CEO is alarmed, especially since the airline's main competitors have not reported similar declines. She has hired us to figure out what's driving the drop and what Skyward should do about it.
prompt.initialQuestion: Why has Skyward Airlines' profitability declined, and what should the CEO do about it?

exhibits.title: Cost Breakdown by Category (Current Year)
exhibits.description: Where Skyward's $1.11B in operating costs goes, vs. the prior year.
exhibits.note: Fuel price per gallon rose ~22% year over year industry-wide due to global oil price increases. Skyward does not currently hedge fuel costs.

exhibits.description: How Skyward compares to two direct competitors on the same routes.

cases.title: Meridian Coffee Co.: Entering Mexico
cases.summary: A premium US coffee chain with 400 stores is considering Mexico as its first international market.

prompt.context: Meridian Coffee Co. operates 400 premium coffee shops across the United States, generating $850M in annual revenue. Domestic growth has slowed to 2% per year as the US market matures. The CEO is considering international expansion and has identified Mexico as a candidate for Meridian's first market outside the US, given geographic proximity and growing urban middle-class demand for premium coffee. She has asked us to evaluate the opportunity before committing capital.
prompt.initialQuestion: Should Meridian Coffee Co. enter the Mexican market? If so, how should they approach it?
